senses.definition: Untamed; not domesticated.

subsenses.definition: Especially, being of the wild type: being of an unbroken ancestral line of undomesticated animals, as opposed to being feral, being an undomesticated animal whose ancestors were domesticated.
examples: Near-synonym: indigenous
Przewalski's horses are the only remaining wild horses, although there are many feral horses throughout the world.
In this region, the wild boars can be dangerous, but (perhaps counterintuitively) the feral hogs can be even worse.

subsenses.definition: Being in the wild, by any pathway (whether by being of the wild type, by being feral since birth, or by being feral after escape from domesticated life).

senses.definition: From or relating to wild creatures.
examples: wild honey

senses.definition: Unrestrained or uninhibited.
examples: I was filled with wild rage when I discovered the infidelity, and punched a hole in the wall.

senses.definition: Raucous, unruly, or licentious.
examples: The fraternity was infamous for its wild parties, which frequently resulted in police involvement.

senses.definition: (electrical engineering) Of unregulated and varying frequency.
examples: The aircraft's navigational equipment should not be powered from the wild AC bus except in an emergency, as its computers can be damaged by variations in electrical frequency.

senses.definition: Visibly and overtly anxious; frantic.
examples: Her mother was wild with fear when she didn't return home after the party.

senses.definition: Furious; very angry.
Disheveled, tangled, or untidy.
examples: After a week on the trail without a mirror, my hair was wild and dirty.

senses.definition: Enthusiastic.
examples: I'm not wild about the idea of a two day car trip with my nephews, but it's my only option.

senses.definition: Very inaccurate; far off the mark.
examples: The novice archer fired a wild shot and hit her opponent's target.

senses.definition: Exposed to the wind and sea; unsheltered.
examples: a wild roadstead

senses.definition: (nautical, of a vessel) Hard to steer.
(mathematics, of a knot) Not capable of being represented as a finite closed polygonal chain.
(slang) Amazing, awesome, unbelievable.
examples: Did you hear? Pat won the lottery! — Wow, that's wild!

senses.definition: (slang) Very unexpected; wildly surprising; crazy, diabolical.
Able to stand in for others, e.g. a card in games, or a text character in computer pattern matching.
examples: In this card game, aces are wild: they can take the place of any other card.

quotes.text: We define a pattern as a valid GP subtree that might contain wild characters [i.e. wildcards] in any of its nodes.

senses.definition: Of an audio recording: intended to be synchronized with film or video but recorded separately.
examples: a wild track; wild sound

senses.definition: Inaccurately; not on target.
examples: The javelin flew wild and struck a spectator, to the horror of all observing.

senses.definition: (of an audio recording) Intended to be synchronized with film or video but recorded separately.
examples: Let's record it wild.

senses.definition: (singular, with "the") The undomesticated state of a wild animal.
examples: After mending the lion's leg, we returned him to the wild.

senses.definition: (chiefly in the plural) A wilderness.
examples:
1730–1774, Oliver Goldsmith, Introductory to Switzerland
Thus every good his native wilds impart
Imprints the patriot passion on his heart;
And e’en those ills that round his mansion rise
Enhance the bliss his scanty funds supplies.

senses.definition: Something that is able to stand in for others, such as a particular playing card in a game.
(intransitive, slang) To commit random acts of assault, robbery, and rape in an urban setting, especially as a gang.
examples: Now is they wildin with us / And getting rowdy with us.
